observations: Alphabet's AI/cloud demand is causally coupled to compute infrastructure, electricity supply, grid interconnection and data-center construction; the announced Intersect acquisition is a direct attempt to internalize part of the energy-development bottleneck.

The chain is user/enterprise AI demand -> compute workload -> accelerator/data-center capacity -> electricity and interconnection -> Alphabet cloud/service delivery. Multi-GW energy-development capability can reduce a binding infrastructure constraint but does not remove permitting, transmission or equipment bottlenecks.
Successor bottlenecks include power equipment, transmission/interconnection, permitting, cooling and the pace at which AI monetization absorbs deployed infrastructure.

Intersect energy-development capability -> potential faster power availability -> cloud/AI capacity
falsifiers: AI monetization persistently fails to absorb infrastructure growth

observations: Large planned infrastructure spending creates duration and return-on-capital risk if monetization trails deployment.
Vertical expansion into energy development can reduce dependency but also adds permitting, construction and power-market execution domains outside Alphabet's historical core.
Rapid model and accelerator changes can shorten useful-life assumptions; this is a scenario risk, not evidence that current infrastructure is impaired.
